audit.title: Claude Code Six Tool Technical Implementation Audit
audit.scope_note: Technical implementation only. No legal, tax, rate, threshold, formula or Product Rule correctness was assessed or asserted.

detail.note: Manifest names v1.5.6; repo HEAD carries v1.4.3. The manifest-named blob exists in git history at commit cb8cfe7 and was audited separately.

findings.summary: The 3-2 artifact in the repository is not the artifact named in the audit manifest.
findings.evidence: Manifest specifies 789,817 bytes / SHA-256 a2558513357b1fbb2081b430b0053cd35fcdaceaceeb2e5bc2419643cab7324f. Repository HEAD (dd81fdc) 3-2/index.html is 597,913 bytes / SHA-256 e60122e51fb315730c429f6b6732e26ec8f10f17ae71da0ae711b1ecce4b5472. 3-2/README.md and DEPLOYMENT.md both state Current Release v1.4.3 with status DEPLOYED / PUBLIC SMOKE PENDING. git log for 3-2/index.html shows: b11d9c2 (v1.4.3) -> cb8cfe7 'Deploy 3-2 v1.5.6 final runtime' -> 88fd381 'Rollback 3-2 production to v1.4.3 after v1.5.6 live search regression'. The manifest-named blob is reachable at cb8cfe7:3-2/index.html and its SHA-256 matches the manifest exactly.
findings.reproduction: git rev-parse HEAD; sha256sum 3-2/index.html; git rev-list --all -- 3-2/index.html; git cat-file blob $(git rev-parse cb8cfe7:3-2/index.html) | sha256sum
findings.why_it_matters: The manifest pins the audit to a version that production has deliberately rolled back. Auditing the repository artifact without saying so would silently report on a different build than the one commissioned; auditing only the manifest version would report on a build that is not live. Neither substitution is safe, so both were audited and are reported separately.
findings.recommended_remediation: Decide which build is the audit subject of record and reissue the manifest line for 3-2 with the matching size and hash. If v1.4.3 is the intended production build, the manifest should name it; if v1.5.6 is to return, finding T32B-01 must be resolved first.
findings.required_regression: A release-time check that the hash recorded in any audit or release manifest equals the hash of the artifact at the referenced commit.

findings.summary: In the manifest-named v1.5.6 build, common single-item queries return a disambiguation prompt instead of results; the deployed v1.4.3 returns results for the same queries.
findings.evidence: Same harness, same queries, two builds. v1.4.3: '停車' -> heading '找到 2 項結果' (3 result nodes); '汽車' -> '找到 1 項結果' (2 nodes); '員工旅遊' -> '找到 1 項結果' (2 nodes). v1.5.6: all three -> heading '先確認搜尋方向' with 1 node and no item results. '餐費' returns 5 hits in both builds, and 'zzz不存在' returns '找不到符合的項目' in both, so the input path itself is functional in both builds.
findings.reproduction: Serve each build over HTTP; type each term into #q; wait 500ms; read document.body.dataset.state, #resultHeading textContent and #results child count. Script: audit_harness/scripts/flows4.js.
findings.why_it_matters: The regression converts a direct answer into an extra decision step for the most common lookups in a lookup tool. It independently corroborates the reason recorded in the rollback commit, and it is the blocking defect for any future re-release of the v1.5.6 line.
findings.recommended_remediation: Treat the routing/disambiguation layer added in v1.5.6 as the regression site. Whether '停車' should resolve directly or disambiguate is a product decision; the technical requirement is that the chosen behaviour be covered by a fixed query-to-outcome test set before re-release.
findings.required_regression: A query-to-outcome table (query -> expected state, expected heading class, expected result count) executed against every 3-2 build.
findings.product_sot_dependency: YES — the correct target behaviour for ambiguous queries is a product rule, not derivable from the code.

findings.summary: After a successful calculation, entering an invalid or empty value and pressing 計算 leaves the previous result on screen unchanged, with no error and no indication that it is stale.
findings.evidence: Single page session, employee path. Enter 45800, click #goEmp -> #res shows 對應投保級距 45,800 / 人事成本 54,879 / 帳面月薪 45,800. Then enter 'abc' and click 計算 -> #res still shows 45,800 / 54,879 / 45,800, class remains 'result on', #eSal has no aria-invalid attribute and no error node is rendered. Identical outcome for '-5', '0' and empty string. Separately: after a valid calculation, editing #eSal to 88888 without clicking 計算 also leaves the 45,800 result displayed with no staleness cue.
findings.reproduction: audit_harness/scripts/t22.js, section 'SEQUENCE ON ONE PAGE'. On a fresh load the same invalid inputs correctly produce no result at all (#res class has no 'on'), which confirms the calculation is being refused — only the display is not being cleared.
findings.why_it_matters: The displayed figures are payroll cost numbers. A user who corrects or clears the salary field and re-runs sees numbers that belong to a value no longer in the field, and nothing on screen distinguishes that from a fresh answer. The refusal logic already exists and works on first load; only the reset of the output region is missing.
findings.recommended_remediation: On every 計算 invocation, clear #res and remove the 'on' class before validating, so a refused calculation cannot leave prior output visible. Additionally surface the refusal (error text plus aria-invalid on #eSal) rather than failing silently.
findings.required_regression: Sequence test: valid input -> assert result present; invalid input -> assert result region empty or explicitly marked stale, and assert an error message is exposed.
findings.product_sot_dependency: NO — this is display-state consistency, independent of which values are valid.

findings.summary: 4-3 has no DOCTYPE declaration and renders in quirks mode.
findings.evidence: The file begins '<meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" ...' with no '<!DOCTYPE html>' and no <html> element. At runtime document.compatMode === 'BackCompat' at 1200, 768, 390 and 320 CSS px. The other five tools all report 'CSS1Compat'.
findings.reproduction: head -c 200 4-3/index.html; and in the browser, document.compatMode. Recorded in audit_harness/results/runtime_report.json.
findings.why_it_matters: Quirks mode changes foundational layout behaviour (table cell and inline box metrics, percentage height resolution, style inheritance into tables). 4-3 is the most table-dependent of the six tools. No visual defect was reproduced in the tested Chromium build, so the present impact is unquantified rather than nil; the exposure is that the layout of the largest production artifact rests on a non-standard document mode across the browsers the public site actually serves. The fix is one line, but it changes layout mode and therefore requires a full visual re-check.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add '<!DOCTYPE html>' and wrap the document in <html lang="zh-Hant-TW"> ... </html>, then re-verify layout at all four widths, because switching to standards mode will change table and inline metrics.
findings.required_regression: Assert document.compatMode === 'CSS1Compat' for every tool, plus a layout snapshot at the four audited widths.

findings.summary: 4-3 declares no document language.
findings.evidence: document.documentElement.lang is null at runtime; the file has no <html> element at all. The other five tools declare zh-Hant or zh-Hant-TW.
findings.reproduction: In the browser: document.documentElement.lang. Recorded in audit_harness/results/runtime_report.json.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen readers select voice and pronunciation rules from the document language; without it, Traditional Chinese content may be announced with the wrong locale. It also affects font selection and hyphenation defaults.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add lang="zh-Hant-TW" to the <html> element introduced with the DOCTYPE fix in T43-01.
findings.required_regression: Assert documentElement.lang is non-empty for every tool.

findings.summary: 4-3 uses native alert(), confirm() and prompt() as its entire error, confirmation and recovery interface — 19 call sites, including a prompt() that asks the user to type a YYYY-MM value.
findings.evidence: 19 matches for /\b(alert|confirm|prompt)\s*\(/ in the application script (4-3_script2.js; the vendor bundle was excluded). Observed live during import testing: alert '這個檔案讀不出來…', alert '檔案結構異常，為安全起見不予載入。', alert '第 1 列第 1 個月的數字不合法…', confirm '確定要清空所有數字？此動作無法復原。', and prompt '這是舊版進度檔，沒有記錄月份基準。請輸入『原資料當時的本月』，格式 YYYY-MM…'.
findings.reproduction: audit_harness/scripts/t43.js, sections 'MALFORMED / HOSTILE IMPORT' and 'CLEAR / RESET'; dialogs captured via page.on('dialog').
findings.why_it_matters: Native dialogs block the main thread, cannot be styled or made to match the tool's visual language, and are inconsistently presented on mobile browsers; prompt() in particular is suppressed or degraded in several mobile engines, which would strand a user on the legacy-file recovery path. The recovery logic behind these dialogs is sound — only its delivery mechanism is fragile.
findings.recommended_remediation: Replace with in-page dialog elements carrying focus management and aria-live announcements. The prompt() path deserves priority because a suppressed prompt has no fallback.
findings.required_regression: Assert no native dialog fires on the import, clear and legacy-recovery paths, and that an equivalent in-page message is present and announced.

findings.summary: A full SheetJS 0.18.5 bundle (639,125 bytes, 84% of the file) is inlined, but only three write-side helpers are used.
findings.evidence: <script id="sheetjs-vendor" data-version="0.18.5"> contains 639,125 bytes; the file total is 1,011,643 bytes. Application usage across the whole app script is limited to XLSX.utils.book_new / book_append_sheet (2 call sites), XLSX.utils.aoa_to_sheet and XLSX.writeFile. No XLSX.read, XLSX.readFile or sheet_to_json call exists, so the parser is never entered. The tool's only file import path is JSON via FileReader, not XLSX.
findings.reproduction: grep -oE 'XLSX[a-zA-Z.]*' on audit_harness/results/extracted/4-3_script2.js; byte counts from audit_harness/results/extract_report.json.
findings.why_it_matters: 0.18.5 predates the fixes for the publicly known SheetJS advisories, which are in the file-reading path. Because no read entry point is reachable from this application, no exploitable path was identified here, and severity is set accordingly. What remains is that a pinned, outdated, unreachable-but-present parser accounts for most of the download weight of the largest tool, and its version will keep appearing in any dependency scan.
findings.recommended_remediation: Either upgrade the pinned bundle, or replace it with a write-only sheet emitter. Tool 4-1 already contains a self-contained ~200-line XLSX writer that produces a valid workbook; reusing it here would remove the vendor bundle entirely. See cross-tool pattern CT-04.
findings.required_regression: Assert the exported .xlsx opens as a valid OOXML package and that expected cells and formulas are present, whichever writer is used.

findings.summary: 87 selectors are declared more than once in the same cascade context and re-declare the same properties, with !important used to win the resulting conflicts.
findings.evidence: Media-aware cascade analysis of the concatenated <style> blocks: 536 rules, 99 same-selector-same-context repeats, 87 re-declaring at least one identical property. Worked example — 'tr.section td' appears in four layers: (1) background:var(--blue);color:#fff;font-weight:700;padding:7px 12px, (2) background:var(--brand-navy-700);padding:8px 12px;border-color:...;box-shadow:inset 3px 0 0 var(--brand-gold-500), (3) border-top:5px solid #fff!important;border-bottom:2px solid var(--brand-gold-500)!important, (4) border-top-width:4px!important.
findings.reproduction: Brace-depth CSS walker recording each rule's @-rule context, then grouping by context+selector and counting repeated property names. Script inline in the audit run; extracted CSS at audit_harness/results/extracted/4-3_all.css.
findings.why_it_matters: Layers 1 and 2 of that example are wholly or partly dead, and layers 3 and 4 need !important only because of the conflict. Any future style edit has to be made in the last winning layer, which is not discoverable from reading the first. This is accumulated-revision residue, not a rendering defect: no visual breakage was observed.
findings.recommended_remediation: Collapse each selector to a single declaration site per cascade context and remove the !important that exists only to defeat an earlier duplicate.
findings.required_regression: A build-time or CI check that flags same-context duplicate selectors re-declaring identical properties.

findings.summary: Two form controls have no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Of 76 fields, two resolve to no label: a type=text input with no id, no name, no aria-label, no title, no wrapping <label> and no label[for]; and input#file (the progress-file picker).
findings.reproduction: Runtime label resolution check in audit_harness/scripts/runtime.js (fieldsUnlabelled).
findings.why_it_matters: An unnamed control is announced only by its role, so a screen-reader user cannot tell what it does. input#file is visually hidden and driven by a labelled button, which mitigates it in practice; the unnamed text input does not have that mitigation.
findings.recommended_remediation: Give the text input an aria-label describing its cell, and an aria-label or aria-hidden treatment to input#file consistent with its button trigger.
findings.required_regression: Assert every rendered form control resolves to a non-empty accessible name.

findings.summary: Currency cells accept arbitrary-precision decimals; 3.14159 is treated as valid and does not suspend autosave.
findings.evidence: Entering 'abc', '-100', '1e5' and '999999999999999999' into a grid cell each set one cell invalid and switched the save indicator to '有錯誤輸入，暫停自動保存（已保留上一版）'. Entering '3.14159' left invalid count at 0 and the indicator at '已自動保存'.
findings.reproduction: audit_harness/scripts/t43.js, section 'INVALID INPUT + AUTOSAVE GUARD'.
findings.why_it_matters: The validator deliberately rejects four other malformed classes, so decimal precision appears to be an intentional allowance rather than an oversight. Whether sub-dollar precision is acceptable in a NT$ cash-flow cell is a product decision this audit cannot make from the code.
findings.recommended_remediation: Confirm the intended precision domain for currency cells against the product contract, then either constrain it or document the allowance. Note the same open question in 2-2 (T22-05) and the contrasting 2-decimal cap in 4-1.
findings.required_regression: Once the domain is fixed, a boundary table per input class (negative, non-numeric, scientific notation, overflow, decimal precision).
findings.product_sot_dependency: YES — the acceptable precision for currency input is an external product rule.

findings.summary: 2-2 has no user-visible validation feedback layer; invalid input is a silent no-op.
findings.evidence: For inputs 'abc', '1e5', '-5', '0' and whitespace on a fresh load, #res never gains the 'on' class, #eSal never receives aria-invalid, and no error node is rendered anywhere in the document. The user sees the 計算 button do nothing. By contrast 4-1 sets aria-invalid="true" and renders a specific message for each rejection class.
findings.reproduction: audit_harness/scripts/t22.js, section 'FRESH PAGE PER INPUT'.
findings.why_it_matters: A control that silently does nothing is indistinguishable from a broken control. This is also the mechanism that makes T22-01 possible: because there is no failure surface, a refused calculation has nowhere to report itself and the previous result simply stays.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add the validation-feedback pattern already implemented in 4-1 (per-field error node, aria-invalid, aria-describedby) to 2-2's inputs.
findings.required_regression: Per-input-class assertions that a rejection sets aria-invalid and renders a message.
findings.product_sot_dependency: NO — the presence of a feedback mechanism is independent of which values are valid.

findings.summary: Twelve interactive controls are smaller than 24x24 CSS px at every tested width, including 13x13 px radio inputs and 48x14 px inline links.
findings.evidence: Measured at 1200, 768, 390 and 320 px: 12 controls under 24 px in either dimension and 12 under 44 px. Examples: INPUT 13x13 (radio, repeated), A '見備註 3' 48x14, A '見備註 5' 48x14. Confirmed reachable by real keyboard tabbing, so these are live controls, not decorative. The other five tools report zero controls under 24 px.
findings.reproduction: getBoundingClientRect over all enabled, visible interactive elements at each width — audit_harness/scripts/runtime.js (subOptimalTargets); cross-checked by keyboard sweep in audit_harness/scripts/flows2.js (tinyFocusable).
findings.why_it_matters: 13x13 px is well under any common minimum touch target and these radios select the insurance role that drives the whole calculation. The '見備註' links are 14 px tall and sit inline in body text, so they are hard to hit without zooming on a phone.
findings.recommended_remediation: Enlarge the radio hit area (a padded label wrapper or a pseudo-element hit box) and give the inline note links vertical padding, without changing the visual design.
findings.required_regression: Assert every interactive element measures at least 24x24 px (preferably 44x44) at 390 and 320 px.

findings.summary: select#bRole has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Of 35 fields, select#bRole is the only one that resolves to no label: no label[for="bRole"], no wrapping <label>, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title.
findings.reproduction: Runtime label resolution check in audit_harness/scripts/runtime.js.
findings.why_it_matters: The remaining 34 fields are labelled, so this is a single omission in an otherwise well-labelled form rather than a systemic gap; a screen-reader user reaching it hears only the role and its current option.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add a label[for="bRole"] or aria-label matching its visible heading.
findings.required_regression: Assert every rendered form control resolves to a non-empty accessible name.

findings.summary: No lower or upper bound is applied to the salary input; 0.4 and 999,999,999 are both accepted and produce results.
findings.evidence: Input 0.4 -> 對應投保級距 29,500, 帳面月薪 0.4 元, 人事成本 5,849.4 元. Input 28590.7 -> 帳面月薪 28,590.7 元, 人事成本 34,439.7 元. Input 999999999 -> 對應投保級距 313,000 (bracket does cap), 帳面月薪 999,999,999 元, 人事成本 1,000,028,317 元.
findings.reproduction: audit_harness/scripts/t22.js, section 'FRESH PAGE PER INPUT'.
findings.why_it_matters: The bracket lookup clearly has a ceiling, so the bracket side of the calculation is bounded; the echoed salary and derived cost figures are not. Whether the tool should refuse out-of-range salaries, or display them as entered, depends on the insurance bracket rules and the intended teaching use, neither of which is in this repository.
findings.recommended_remediation: Obtain the intended input domain (minimum, maximum, decimal places) from the product contract, then enforce it through the feedback layer added in T22-02.
findings.required_regression: Boundary table once the domain is fixed: below minimum, at minimum, at maximum, above maximum, and decimal precision.
findings.product_sot_dependency: YES — the valid salary domain and bracket ceiling are external rules; this audit does not assert what they are.

findings.summary: The production page title contains an internal release-process label: 「地址登記決策工具｜v2.1.2 Remediation Candidate」.
findings.evidence: <title>地址登記決策工具｜v2.1.2 Remediation Candidate</title>; confirmed at runtime as document.title at all four widths. DEPLOYMENT.md records 2-1 as v2.1.2 with status LIVE.
findings.reproduction: grep '<title>' 2-1/index.html; document.title in the browser.
findings.why_it_matters: The title is the most externally visible string a page has: it is the browser tab text, the default bookmark name, the share-card title and the search result heading. A live tool published under the practitioner's own brand describes itself to visitors as a remediation candidate. The other five titles carry no such label.
findings.recommended_remediation: Set the title to the tool's public name only, matching the pattern used by 1-1, 2-2 and 3-2 (name｜聖彥學堂), and keep version identity in README.md, DEPLOYMENT.md and the commit history where it already lives.
findings.required_regression: Assert no page title matches /candidate|draft|rc|remediation|test/i.

findings.summary: 2-1 contains no heading elements at all; question and result titles are styled non-heading elements.
findings.evidence: grep -c for <h1>..<h6> over 2-1/index.html returns 0. At runtime the heading collection is empty and h1 count is 0 at all four widths. Visual headings are carried by classes .q-title, .result-title, .progress-heading, .fact-title, .brand-title. All five other tools expose exactly one <h1> plus a nested structure with no level skips.
findings.reproduction: grep -c '<h1\|<h2\|<h3\|<h4\|<h5\|<h6' 2-1/index.html; and in the browser, document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,h4,h5,h6').length.
findings.why_it_matters: Heading navigation is a primary way screen-reader users move through a page; with no headings there is nothing to navigate by, and the current question — the single most important string on screen at any moment — has no programmatic prominence. The page has a <main> landmark, so the fix is confined to element choice.
findings.recommended_remediation: Promote .q-title / .result-title to <h1> (or <h2> under a page <h1>) and the section titles to the matching level, keeping the existing classes so the visual design is unchanged.
findings.required_regression: Assert each tool exposes exactly one <h1> and a heading outline with no skipped levels.

findings.summary: 48 selectors are declared twice in the base cascade context and re-declare the same properties.
findings.evidence: 288 rules, 50 same-context repeats, 48 re-declaring identical properties. Examples: '.opt' declared twice re-declaring display, width, text-align, font-size, color, background; '.btn' twice re-declaring padding, border, background, color, border-radius, cursor; 'body' twice re-declaring font-family, background, color, line-height, padding.
findings.reproduction: Media-aware cascade analysis over audit_harness/results/extracted/2-1_all.css.
findings.why_it_matters: '.opt' and '.btn' are the tool's only interactive controls, and their first declaration is entirely overridden. Editing the first block has no effect, which is a maintenance trap rather than a rendering defect; nothing visually broken was observed.
findings.recommended_remediation: Merge each selector into one declaration site per context.
findings.required_regression: CI check flagging same-context duplicate selectors re-declaring identical properties.

findings.summary: All interaction is wired through inline onclick attributes calling global functions; the tool registers zero addEventListener handlers.
findings.evidence: 10 inline on* handler attributes and 0 addEventListener calls in 2-1's script. Handlers are emitted into innerHTML strings, e.g. nav.innerHTML = '<button type="button" class="btn" onclick="back()">上一題</button>' ... Runtime check confirms window.answer, window.back and window.restart are all functions. 2-2, 3-2, 4-1 and 4-3 use addEventListener (8 to 26 registrations each); 1-1 mixes both (4 inline, 1 listener).
findings.reproduction: Static counts in audit_harness/results/static_report.json; runtime typeof check in audit_harness/scripts/flows3.js.
findings.why_it_matters: The behaviour is correct and every flow tested passes, so this is a consistency and hardening observation rather than a defect. It does mean the tool cannot run under a Content-Security-Policy that forbids inline handlers, and it keeps three function names in the global namespace where any later script could shadow them.
findings.recommended_remediation: If CSP hardening is ever wanted for the tool site, convert to delegated listeners keyed on data attributes, as 3-2 already does. Otherwise record as accepted.
findings.required_regression: None required while the current approach is accepted; if converted, re-run the wizard path test.

findings.summary: In-file version strings (v3.6.2, v3.6.0) do not match the released version v3.6.4.
findings.evidence: The only semantic version strings in 1-1/index.html are v3.6.2 (twice) and v3.6.0 (once). DEPLOYMENT.md and the manifest both record the release as v3.6.4, and the file hash matches the manifest exactly, so this is the correct artifact carrying stale internal labels. The same pattern appears in 4-1 (T41-04).
findings.reproduction: grep -oE 'v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' 1-1/index.html | sort | uniq -c
findings.why_it_matters: Anyone reading the artifact to determine which build they have is told 3.6.2. Version identity is currently authoritative only in DEPLOYMENT.md and git; the in-file strings drift silently because nothing checks them.
findings.recommended_remediation: Either update in-file version strings at release time or remove them so DEPLOYMENT.md and git remain the single source of version truth. Removing them is the cheaper option and matches 2-2, which carries no version string at all.
findings.required_regression: If in-file versions are kept, a release check that every in-file version string equals the DEPLOYMENT.md release for that tool.

findings.summary: 1-1 mixes inline onclick attributes with addEventListener.
findings.evidence: 4 inline on* attributes (onclick="pick('q1','yes')", back(), restart()) alongside 1 addEventListener registration.
findings.reproduction: Static counts in audit_harness/results/static_report.json.
findings.why_it_matters: Two wiring conventions in one 993-line file means a maintainer must check both places to find where a control is handled. All flows tested pass, so this is maintainability only.
findings.recommended_remediation: Settle on one convention per tool; see cross-tool pattern CT-03.
findings.required_regression: None while accepted.

findings.summary: An entire legacy design-token palette is dead: all 18 custom properties in the first :root block are redeclared with different values in a second :root block.
findings.evidence: Two :root blocks in the base cascade context (18 and 42 custom properties). All 18 names in the first block reappear in the second with different values, so none of the first block's values ever apply. Examples: --navy '#1F3864' -> 'var(--brand-navy-900)'; --red '#C00000' -> 'var(--danger-700)'; --ink '#14181F' -> 'var(--ink-900)'; --bg '#FFFFFF' -> 'var(--paper-50)'; --red-mid '#F3D2D2' -> '#E7B7B1'.
findings.reproduction: Extract both :root blocks from audit_harness/results/extracted/4-1_all.css and diff the custom property maps.
findings.why_it_matters: The file contains two complete and conflicting colour systems, of which only the later one is live. A maintainer editing --navy in the first block would see no change and no error. This is the clearest instance of the accumulated-revision residue that also affects 2-1 and 4-3.
findings.recommended_remediation: Delete the superseded :root block once confirmed that no other stylesheet or inline style depends on the raw hex values.
findings.required_regression: Visual snapshot at the four audited widths before and after removal to prove the palette is genuinely unused.

findings.summary: The reset control discards all user input without confirmation, and the tool has no persistence layer to recover from.
findings.evidence: button#resetBtn 「回到課程範例數字」. Enter 777 in #price, click #resetBtn -> #price returns to 500 immediately, with no dialog captured by page.on('dialog'). localStorage remains empty at every point in the session (0 keys), so nothing can be recovered. For contrast, 4-3's equivalent 清空重填 raises confirm('確定要清空所有數字？此動作無法復原。') and 4-3 autosaves continuously.
findings.reproduction: Load 4-1, fill #price, click #resetBtn, read #price and captured dialogs. Recorded in audit_harness/results/t41_log.txt and the follow-up verification run.
findings.why_it_matters: 4-1 collects a full cost model — asset rows, eight fixed-cost rows, three variable-cost rows, price, volume and target profit. One click on a control whose label reads as a navigation action ('回到課程範例數字') discards all of it irreversibly. Note that the button does work as designed; the gap is the absence of a confirmation step and of any recovery path.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add a confirmation step to the reset control. Adopting 4-3's autosave pattern would also close the wider gap noted in CT-05, but the confirmation alone addresses this finding.
findings.required_regression: Assert the reset control requires confirmation and that declining it leaves all inputs unchanged.

findings.summary: 82 selectors are declared more than once in the same cascade context and re-declare the same properties.
findings.evidence: 520 rules, 89 same-context repeats, 82 re-declaring identical properties, including the :root case reported separately as T41-01. Further examples: '.scope' twice re-declaring margin-top, padding, border-radius, background, border, border-left; 'section' twice re-declaring margin-top, padding, border, border-radius, background; '.quick-nav a.qn-advanced::after' three times re-declaring content, padding, border-radius, background, color, font-size. The tool also carries 12 @media blocks with max-width:600px, 380px and 430px each appearing twice.
findings.reproduction: Media-aware cascade analysis over audit_harness/results/extracted/4-1_all.css.
findings.why_it_matters: 4-1 has the highest duplicate density of the six tools after 4-3. No rendering defect was observed; the cost is that the live value of a property is not discoverable by reading the first declaration.
findings.recommended_remediation: Collapse duplicate selectors and merge the repeated media blocks into one per breakpoint.
findings.required_regression: CI check flagging same-context duplicate selectors re-declaring identical properties.

findings.summary: In-file version strings are inconsistent with the released version: v1.6.6 appears three times against a release of v1.6.7.
findings.evidence: Version strings present: v1.6.6 (x3), v1.6.7 (x1), plus a changelog trail of v1.6.1, v1.5.5, v1.5.4, v1.5.3, v1.5.2, v1.5.1. DEPLOYMENT.md records v1.6.7. The file hash matches the manifest exactly.
findings.reproduction: grep -oE 'v?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' 4-1/index.html | sort | uniq -c
findings.why_it_matters: The dominant in-file version string is not the released one, so a reader inspecting the artifact draws the wrong conclusion. Same root cause as T11-01.
findings.recommended_remediation: As T11-01: update at release time or remove in-file version strings entirely.
findings.required_regression: If kept, a release check tying in-file version strings to DEPLOYMENT.md.

findings.summary: 4-1 exposes no <main> landmark.
findings.evidence: Runtime landmark counts at 1200 px: 4-1 {main:0, nav:1, header:1, footer:0}; 2-2 {main:0, ...}; 4-3 {main:0, ...}. 1-1, 2-1 and 3-2 each expose main:1.
findings.reproduction: document.querySelectorAll('main,[role=main]').length — audit_harness/scripts/runtime.js.
findings.why_it_matters: Skip-to-content and landmark navigation have no target. 4-1 does have a good heading outline (one h1, no level skips), so the loss is limited to landmark navigation. Three of six tools share this gap, tracked as CT-02.
findings.recommended_remediation: Wrap the primary content region in <main> in 4-1, 2-2 and 4-3.
findings.required_regression: Assert every tool exposes exactly one main landmark.

findings.summary: No tool declares a meta description, favicon or theme-color.
findings.evidence: All six files: name="description" absent, rel="icon"/apple-touch-icon absent, name="theme-color" absent.
findings.reproduction: grep for each meta/link across the six files.
findings.why_it_matters: These are publicly linked tools on GitHub Pages with a branded custom domain pending. Without a description, search engines and social shares synthesise their own summary; without a favicon, browsers show a default glyph and issue a 404-producing /favicon.ico probe. Low impact, uniformly absent, and cheap to fix in one pass.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add a one-line description, a shared favicon and a theme-color to all six, ideally from one shared header snippet.
findings.required_regression: Assert presence of description, icon and theme-color per tool.

findings.summary: Three of six tools expose no <main> landmark; landmark usage is inconsistent across the set.
findings.evidence: main present in 1-1, 2-1, 3-2; absent in 2-2, 4-1, 4-3. header present in 2-2, 3-2, 4-1, 4-3; absent in 1-1, 2-1. footer present only in 2-2 and 3-2. nav present only in 4-1.
findings.reproduction: Runtime landmark counts in audit_harness/results/runtime_report.json.
findings.why_it_matters: Because the six tools share a brand and are linked from one index, a screen-reader user moving between them meets a different document skeleton each time. No single instance is severe.
findings.recommended_remediation: Agree one landmark skeleton (header / main / footer) and apply it to all six.
findings.required_regression: Assert the agreed landmark set per tool.

findings.summary: Event wiring, state persistence and validation strategy differ per tool with no shared convention, and no tool ever removes a listener.
findings.evidence: Event wiring: 2-1 fully inline (10 inline, 0 listeners); 1-1 mixed (4 inline, 1 listener); 2-2, 3-2, 4-1, 4-3 use listeners only (26, 8, 18, 16). removeEventListener count is 0 in all six, while innerHTML re-render assignments range from 6 to 18 per tool. Persistence: only 4-3 persists (localStorage key 'cashflow-budget-v7'); the other five hold state in memory only. Validation: 4-1 and 4-3 have explicit per-field validators with messages; 2-2 has none (T22-02).
findings.reproduction: audit_harness/results/static_report.json; runtime localStorage inspection per tool.
findings.why_it_matters: No listener leak was demonstrated — the re-render targets and the listener targets appear to be different elements, so this is recorded as a risk to verify rather than a defect. The wider point is that six tools presented as one family have six different internal conventions, so a fix developed in one does not transfer.
findings.recommended_remediation: Extract the conventions that already work best in the set (4-1's validation layer, 4-3's persistence and import guards, 3-2's delegated listeners) into a shared baseline for new tools and for the next revision of each existing one.
findings.required_regression: A listener-count probe across a full re-render cycle to confirm no accumulation.

findings.summary: The two calculators implement XLSX export twice by entirely different means.
findings.evidence: 4-1 contains a self-contained writer of roughly 200 lines (xlsxEsc, xlsxColName, xlsxSheetXml, xlsxMakeCrcTable, xlsxCrc32, xlsxU16, xlsxU32, xlsxCat, xlsxZipStore) producing a 7-entry, 3-sheet package of 13,018 bytes. 4-3 inlines SheetJS 0.18.5 (639,125 bytes) and calls three helpers, producing a 10-entry package of 22,519 bytes. Both outputs were verified to be valid ZIP archives with well-formed OOXML worksheet and workbook parts (zipfile.testzip OK on both).
findings.reproduction: Trigger both exports via the harness, save the downloads and inspect with Python zipfile — audit_harness/scripts/t41.js and t43.js; artefacts at audit_harness/results/4-1_export.xlsx and 4-3_export.xlsx.
findings.why_it_matters: One capability, two implementations, two maintenance surfaces and two bug classes. It is also the practical route to closing T43-04: 4-1's writer already demonstrates that a valid workbook can be produced without a vendor bundle, at 1/50th of the payload.
findings.recommended_remediation: Choose one export implementation for the tool family. If 4-1's writer is chosen, confirm it covers the formula cells 4-3 emits (4-3 writes SUM and cross-reference formulas, which the 4-1 writer's inline-string and numeric cell paths would need to support) before migrating.
findings.required_regression: One shared export test asserting a valid OOXML package and expected cell and formula content, run for both tools.

findings.summary: The repository contains no automated test or CI infrastructure of any kind.
findings.evidence: 14 tracked files in total: six index.html, six README.md, DEPLOYMENT.md and README.md. No package.json, no test directory, no .github/workflows, no linter or formatter configuration. DEPLOYMENT.md defines release gates in prose ('只有通過 Release Identity Lock 的正式 Runtime 才可部署', 'NOT EXECUTED 不得視為 PASS') with no executable check behind them.
findings.reproduction: git ls-files; find for config and workflow files.
findings.why_it_matters: Every finding in this report was found by ad hoc tooling built for this run and discarded with it. The 3-2 v1.5.6 search regression (T32B-01) reached production and was caught only after live use, which is the failure mode a query-to-outcome test would have prevented at near-zero cost. The tools are self-contained static HTML, which makes them unusually easy to test: no build, no server, no fixtures.
findings.recommended_remediation: Add a minimal Playwright suite plus a GitHub Actions workflow. The highest-value assertions are already specified per finding and are collected in Six_Tool_Test_Inventory.md.
findings.required_regression: This finding is itself the regression infrastructure.

findings.summary: The three numeric tools apply three different and mutually inconsistent input domains.
findings.evidence: 4-1 rejects negatives ('本工具不支援負值，請填 0 或正數'), non-numeric, scientific notation and more than two decimal places ('請輸入一般數字，最多 2 位小數…'), and sets aria-invalid. 4-3 rejects negatives, non-numeric, scientific notation and 18-digit overflow, but accepts 3.14159. 2-2 rejects nothing visibly and accepts 0.4, 28590.7 and 999999999.
findings.reproduction: audit_harness/scripts/t22.js, t41.js and t43.js — the same input classes were applied to each tool.
findings.why_it_matters: All three present currency amounts to the same audience under one brand. A learner who is told in 4-1 that two decimal places is the limit is allowed five in 4-3 and unlimited magnitude in 2-2. Which domain is correct is a product decision; that the three disagree is a technical fact this audit can confirm.
findings.recommended_remediation: Fix one numeric input contract for the tool family (sign, magnitude ceiling, decimal places, rejection presentation), then apply it to all three. 4-1's implementation is the most complete starting point.
findings.required_regression: One shared boundary table applied to every numeric input across all three tools.
findings.product_sot_dependency: YES — the correct domain per field type is an external product rule; this finding asserts only the inconsistency, not which tool is right.

not_reproduced.claim: Duplicate DOM id 'resultHeading' (x2 in v1.4.3, x3 plus 'emptyBrowse' x2 in v1.5.6).
not_reproduced.why: The static scan counted id="resultHeading" occurrences across the whole file including script text. Splitting markup from script shows 0 occurrences in markup and 2 in JavaScript — they are mutually exclusive template branches of the same render function (the no-results branch and the results branch), only one of which is ever inserted. Runtime duplicate-id checks returned an empty set at all four widths and after every search term tested, including the empty-result path.
not_reproduced.lesson: A whole-file id count over a single-file app conflates markup with template strings.

not_reproduced.claim: 23 of 60 focusable elements render no visible focus indicator.
not_reproduced.why: The first probe called element.focus() programmatically. Chromium does not apply :focus-visible to programmatic focus on buttons and links absent prior keyboard interaction, so the computed outline was legitimately 'none 0px'. Re-testing by dispatching real Tab key presses and reading the computed style at each stop returned zero elements without a visible indicator, in all six tools (1-1, 2-1, 2-2, 3-2, 4-1, 4-3). Focus visibility is a strength of this set, not a defect.
not_reproduced.lesson: Focus-visibility must be measured with real key events; programmatic focus produces false positives.

not_reproduced.claim: Console error 'Failed to load resource: 404 (Not Found)' on load.
not_reproduced.why: Appeared only on the first page load of a cold browser process. With a response listener attached before navigation, the total request list for the page is exactly one entry (the document itself) and no response has status >= 400. The static server access log contains no 404 lines for the audit period. Consistent with the browser's own favicon probe, which relates to CT-01 (no favicon declared) rather than to any missing application resource.
not_reproduced.lesson: Cold-start console noise must be re-checked with listeners attached before navigation and against the server log.

not_reproduced.claim: The scenario table (#scenBody) renders seven empty rows.
not_reproduced.why: innerText returned empty strings because the table was inside a region not being rendered at read time. innerHTML on the same node at the same moment shows populated rows: 40%8040,000-30,000 and so on. The table is populated correctly both before and after input.
not_reproduced.lesson: innerText is layout-dependent; assert on innerHTML or textContent for content presence.

not_reproduced.claim: 4-1 provides no reset or clear control.
not_reproduced.why: The control exists as button#resetBtn labelled 「回到課程範例數字」. The first sweep matched labels against /重新|清空|重設/ and missed it. The control works. A separate, real issue with the same control is reported as T41-02 (no confirmation before discarding input).
not_reproduced.lesson: Enumerate controls by role and id, not by expected label text.

not_reproduced.claim: XLSX export writes out-of-bounds column references when the month count exceeds the COL array.
not_reproduced.why: COL is ["B","C","D","E","F","G","H"] (7 entries) and N is a fixed 7. Every loop indexes COL[m] or COL[m-1] for m < N, so the maximum index reached is 6. No out-of-bounds access is possible while N stays 7. The exported workbook was verified valid. Worth noting only as a latent coupling: raising N without extending COL would silently emit 'undefined' cell references.
not_reproduced.lesson: Confirm the loop bound against the array length before reporting an indexing defect.
